rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Decoding Marvel and screen symbolism", "body": "Chance described the Marvelous Demystifiers as a fun way to explore archetypes through Marvel and Disney films, and he argued that reverse engineering programming leads back to truth. He credited the phrase symbolic literacy is psychic self-defense to Michael Tsarion, and said enjoying a film while spotting its encoding was fine. Rob Edward, who has a film and television background, raised Everything Everywhere All at Once, the OA and Stranger Things. Chance suggested the trauma-gives-powers storyline in these shows reflected worldview warfare, and he found the push for a multiverse suspect."}, {"title": "Ether, worldview warfare and health first", "body": "Chance gave an overview in which he described ether as an indivisible medium shared by every body and the whole cosmos, so that a fearful worldview, in his words, shapes the inner state and healing yourself heals the world. He said fear works as a form of consent, and that newcomers to conspiracy research should head toward health first. Rob added that constant next-month doom predictions left people paralyzed, caught in thought without action."}, {"title": "Biofield tuning, the root chakra and livelihood", "body": "Chance described his remote tuning fork sessions and credited biofield anatomy to Eileen Day McKusick, whom he called his unofficial guru. He said stuck energy behind the hips reflected thought that never became action, and that the root chakra related to work, home and fear. He urged people to move toward a resonant livelihood in gradual steps. Rob shared how he began his own show through a leap of faith, and Chance added a note of common sense."}, {"title": "Mystic versus mechanistic, and free will", "body": "Chance said Dylan Saccoccio's books and Wilhelm Reich's writing helped him see the mystic and mechanistic paradigms as two sides asking for trust in experts. He traced the words rapture and dragon to a common idea of being taken away, calling it speculation. He disagreed with the claim that higher beings lack free will, saying free will was synonymous with source. He also said he was working to drop beliefs he had not proven for himself, including his reading of karma."}, {"title": "Love, the zero point and pattern recognition", "body": "Chance proposed that love, at its root, meant honoring potential rather than controlling outcomes, drawing on word play with Jove and the letter L. Later he described a pleroma from Jung, the zero point, and his view that a frequency works through coherence rather than pitch. Rob asked how people could find strength in these times. Chance answered that people could give their mind a new game, noticing when a fear pattern was running instead of hunting for more reasons to fear."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Rob Edward invited me onto the Dig Within Podcast for a wide-ranging conversation about the InnerVerse, Vibe Rant and the Marvelous Demystifiers, including how symbolic literacy changes the way we watch Marvel films, Stranger Things and Everything Everywhere All at Once. We also dug into biofield tuning, the ether and what love might really mean.
